gap: No result ChatGPT got states that on the Anker Prime 100W 3-port charger ChatGPT recommends as its top wall charger, using USB-C2 and USB-A together cuts both ports to 12 W each (24 W total). So in the usual hotel-night setup with no laptop (phone on the second USB-C port, earbuds or watch on USB-A), the phone charges at 12 W, and the phone has to go on C1 to get fast charging.
standout_why: I compared five pages. publicasta.com (cited) says only that a 100 W charger 'might give the laptop 65 W when a phone is also plugged in' and names no products. itechguides.com (cited) gives splits for UGREEN, Satechi, INIU and Amazon Basics but does not cover the Anker Prime 100W. androidauthority.com (cited in the laptop-and-phone chat) gives the Anker Prime 100W split as 65/35 W for two devices and 45/30/12 W for three, and advises keeping power on the primary port. That is part of the finding, but it never says that the C2 + USB-A pair drops to 12 W + 12 W. I could not open wired.com or travelandleisure.com because the fetch was refused, so I can't say whether they cover it. Both are adapter roundups, not charger port tables.
kit_items: Wall charger: for a UGREEN single-store cart, use the UGREEN Nexode 65W 3-Port Travel Charger with US/UK/EU Plug. The swappable heads mean UK and EU trips need no separate plug adapter. If you need 100 W for the laptop, use the UGREEN Nexode 100W 4-Port instead. Avoid ChatGPT's Anker Prime 100W for phone-plus-earbuds nights unless the phone goes on C1, because C2 + USB-A is 12 W + 12 W.

Power bank: the UGREEN 145W 25,000 mAh 3-port bank is 90 Wh, which is under the common 100 Wh carry-on limit, and it puts out 140 W on USB-C1, so it can charge a laptop. UGREEN sells it bundled with two 100 W USB-C cables. For phone-only trips, ChatGPT's Anker Nano 10K 45W with a built-in retractable cable is the light option, but it is Amazon-only.
Cables: two USB-C to USB-C cables rated 100 W. They come in the UGREEN power-bank bundle. Anker's page says the Prime 100W ships with no cable and recommends an e-marker cable for 100 W.

Plug adapter: you only need one beyond the US, UK and EU, for example Australia or Type I countries, which the UGREEN three-head set does not cover. Options are the Baseus EnerCore CG11 70W ($27.99 at Baseus) or the EPICKA 70W GaN ($46.99 on Amazon).
Organizer: ChatGPT suggested the Peak Design Small Tech Pouch at $49.95. It is not sold by any approved store I checked, so I left it out of the carts.
